newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends lower as soybeans falter on exports.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends lower as soybeans falter on exports.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed lower on a drop in soybean futures that was tied to a disappointing weekly export sales number and on fund selling, traders said.
The corn export tally was at a hefty level for the week at 792,400 tonnes but the tally was not surprising.
"Export sales for corn were good but they were expected to be good this time of year," a trader said.

Traders said corn and soybeans were in a seasonal harvest decline and new crop contracts continued to fluctuate near what some perceive to be oversold levels and corn futures appear to be settling into a trading range.
December's nine day relative strength index (RSI) closed at 26.289 points, below oversold status at 30 but well above the recent RSI low of 12.412 points set October 4.
Corn early this week staged a weak recovery with most linking that rise to short term technical buy signals.

"The technical bounce is over and now the seasonal break resumes. The floor is getting short now," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter Reynolds. "We need to see what the numbers look like in the morning."
Corn closed 3-3/4 to 6-1/2 cents per bushel lower, with December down 3-3/4 at $2.90.

At 0730 CDT Friday USDA will release its October crop production report and an average of analysts' estimates placed the 1996 U.S. corn production tally at 8.951 billion bushels. That is above USDA's forcast in September for 8.804 billion bushels and well above 1995 U.S. production at 7.374 billion.
"It will be hard to get a bullish report tomorrow. USDA coming in with a bullish report is not likely and no one wanted to be long going into that report," the trader said.
Corn futures volume was estimated at 40,000, slightly down from 40,195 Wednesday, according to the CBOT.

In corn options, Smith Barney bought 500 December $2.80 puts and sold 500 December $2.90 puts at 3-1/2 cents, traders said. Also, Smith Barney bought 500 March $2.90 puts and sold 500 March $2.80 puts at 3-3/4 cents, sources said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 18,000, down from 18,815 Wednesday.
